title: Self-reported Fitzpatrick type I to VI by race group, using descriptions that name skin colour, women in Philadelphia and San Juan (Sommers et al. 2019)

population.description: 446 English- or Spanish-speaking women aged 21 and over in Philadelphia and San Juan, Puerto Rico, recruited by flyers at health sciences centres for a study of skin injury, and enrolled to match the age and race and ethnicity mix of an existing sexual assault registry. Mean age 32.8.
population.country: United States (Philadelphia) and Puerto Rico (San Juan)
population.exclusions: Women with injury to the genitalia. Of 575 screened, 109 declined.

measurement.method: Self-reported type, chosen in an interview from six descriptions that name a skin colour as well as a sun reaction: "Type I, very fair, always burns, never tans; Type II, fair, burns easily; Type III, fair, sometimes burns; Type IV, beige-olive, burns minimally; Type V, moderate brown, rarely burns; Type VI, dark brown or black, never burns".
measurement.protocol: Read to the participant by a trained research assistant in English or Spanish at a skin research laboratory.

analysis: Shares are the row percentages printed in the paper's Table 1 for each race group, converted to fractions. The paper's three groups are White/White Hispanic, Black/Black Hispanic, and Other Identities.
n for each group is the sum of the six counts printed in that row (178, 68, 200); the paper states the groups only as 40%, 15%, and 45% of the sample.
The whole-sample row of Table 1 is not entered: its printed percentages sum to 100.4, and 36 of 446 is 8.1%, not the 8.5% printed for Type V.
use_for: Showing how the wording of the Fitzpatrick question changes the answer: these descriptions name a skin colour, and 71% of Black or Black Hispanic women chose Type VI.
do_not_use_for: A distribution for any population: a quota-matched convenience sample of women in two cities.
Comparison with sources that asked about sun reaction alone, as if they measured the same thing.
caveats: **Women only, recruited by flyer, in two cities.** Enrolment was matched to the age and race mix of a sexual assault registry, not to any population.
**The paper gives two sample sizes.** The abstract says N=466; the Methods, Results, and tables say 446. 466 is also given as the number enrolled.

**The descriptions mix colour and sun reaction.** "Type VI, dark brown or black, never burns" lets a respondent answer on colour. Sources that ask only about burning and tanning get very different answers from Black respondents.
**Small groups.** The Other Identity group is 68 women.

citation.text: Sommers MS, Fargo JD, Regueira Y, Brown KM, Beacham BL, Perfetti AR, Everett JS, Margolis DJ. Are the Fitzpatrick Skin Phototypes valid for cancer risk assessment in a racially and ethnically diverse sample of women? Ethnicity & Disease. 2019;29(3):505-512.
citation.license: Not stated on the article pages read. Confirm the journal's terms before publishing the transcribed values.

verification: The full article was read by Sentinel on 2026-10-06 from a PDF supplied by Ross Wilkinson. The counts in the three race rows of Table 1 sum to 446 and, by type, to the counts in the table's whole-sample row (21, 54, 143, 54, 36, 138).
